title: Ghost and Drop
premise: Hazel Thornbury, a ghost in the private security world, is confronted by a stranger named Ilya who claims Hazel once saved his life—a favor Hazel has no memory of. The debt comes due when Ilya reveals he possesses the ledger of a dead arms broker, a ledger naming Hazel's real identity and the family Hazel buried to disappear. As a mercenary syndicate closes in to seize the ledger before a dawn extraction flight, Hazel and Ilya form an uneasy alliance that hardens into love, forcing Hazel to choose between erasing the past forever or claiming the inheritance—and the found family—that comes with it. In the end, Hazel trades the ledger's most dangerous secret to the syndicate in exchange for safe passage, boards the flight with Ilya and a makeshift family of strays, and finally lets the ghost die so the person can live.
about_author: Lena Dunmore is the pen name of a former risk consultant who spent a decade writing threat assessments for clients she was never allowed to name. She now writes thrillers from a coastal cottage, drawing on the moral gray zones of contract security work.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Between contracts, Hazel maintains a meticulously invisible life in a Lisbon boarding house—until a stranger, Ilya, appears at the door claiming Hazel saved his life in Mombasa three years ago. Hazel has no memory of it. The beat is unease: someone has studied Hazel too closely, and that is never innocent.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya explains the debt: not money, but a ledger belonging to the dead broker Vasili Krayev, hidden in a bank vault under a name only Ilya knows. He offers Hazel first claim on it—before the syndicate that killed Krayev finds it. The beat is seduction of a dangerous kind: being seen after years of erasure.

chapters.title: Clients Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel runs a routine protection detail for a nervous whistleblower, using it as cover to investigate Ilya's story. Every record of the Mombasa incident has been scrubbed—except one, in Hazel's own encrypted archive, that Hazel never wrote. The beat is dread: the past has been edited, and not by Hazel.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Shadow
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya confesses he was Krayev's courier, and that the ledger lists not just arms deals but the true identities of everyone who ever vanished through Krayev's network—including a name that makes Hazel go white. The beat is revelation withheld; Ilya knows more about Hazel than Hazel does.

chapters.title: Strays
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel assembles a crew for the vault job: Dez, a disgraced locksmith; Marisol, a forger who treats Hazel like a sister; and Tomás, a teenage hacker Hazel informally adopted. The beat is warmth—found family forming around a job none of them should take.

chapters.title: The Syndicate Knocks
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Men from the Voss syndicate visit the boarding house, asking polite questions with impolite eyes. Hazel realizes the syndicate knows the ledger exists and suspects who holds the key. The beat is the noose tightening; invisibility has a countdown now.

chapters.title: Mombasa, Remembered
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, intercut with fragmented memory. Under pressure, Hazel finally recalls Mombasa: a burning convoy, a boy pulled from the wreckage—Krayev's own son, the boy who became Ilya. Hazel saved him and buried the memory to survive. The beat is grief surfacing like a body in water.

chapters.title: The Name in the Vault
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya reveals the ledger contains Hazel's birth name and the location of the family Hazel believes dead—records suggesting a sibling survived. The beat is hope weaponized: the ledger is no longer a job, it's an inheritance.

chapters.title: Vault Under Salt
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The crew breaches the coastal bank vault in a taut, procedural sequence. They get the ledger out—but Dez trips a silent alarm, and the syndicate now has a face to hunt. The beat is triumph curdling instantly into exposure.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Costs
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Reading the ledger by lamplight, the crew learns its true weight: it can topple governments or be sold to them. Voss offers Marisol a fortune to hand it over. The beat is temptation splitting the found family at its seam.

chapters.title: Dez's Price
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Dez, terrified, sells the crew's location to Voss—then, unable to live with it, warns Hazel first and disappears. The beat is betrayal and grace in the same breath; even the weak get to choose once.

chapters.title: Run Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The safehouse burns. Hazel, Ilya, Marisol, and Tomás go mobile through Lisbon's night markets and tram tunnels, one step ahead of Voss's hunters. The beat is kinetic fear shot through with unexpected intimacy between Hazel and Ilya.

chapters.title: The Extraction Flight
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. Tomás finds the only way out: a dawn cargo flight from a disused airstrip, brokered by an old contact of Hazel's who demands a secret as payment. The clock is set: wheels up at first light. The beat is fragile hope with a price tag.

chapters.title: Voss Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Voss corners Hazel alone and offers a trade: the ledger's most dangerous secret—a live arms pipeline—in exchange for safe passage for everyone, no blood. The beat is the devil's arithmetic: one secret worth killing for, weighed against four lives.

chapters.title: Ilya's Truth
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya admits he didn't come for gratitude alone—Krayev's will names him heir to the network, and the ledger legitimizes a claim he isn't sure he wants. He asks Hazel to help him burn it instead. The beat is two ghosts deciding to become people together.

chapters.title: Marisol's Choice
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol, offered Voss's fortune again, forges a decoy ledger instead and slips it to the syndicate, buying the crew hours. The beat is loyalty proven through craftsmanship; the family holds.

chapters.title: The Airstrip
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The crew reaches the airstrip to find Voss's men already there—the decoy failed. A standoff in the fog: guns, the real ledger in Hazel's coat, and the engines warming. The beat is the point of no return.

chapters.title: Trade the Secret
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel makes the trade—handing Voss the pipeline secret, the one thing that could have made Hazel rich and untouchable—in exchange for the crew walking to the plane alive. The beat is sacrifice as identity: Hazel chooses people over power.

chapters.title: Wheels Up at Dawn
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. As the plane lifts into first light, Voss's men hold their word—mostly—and a last-minute betrayal by Dez's handlers forces a desperate takeoff under fire. The beat is exhale and adrenaline: escape earned, not given.

chapters.title: The Sibling
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Over the sea, Hazel opens the ledger's final page and finds the surviving sibling's name and city. Ilya offers to go with Hazel. The beat is trembling hope: the inheritance is not money but a person, still alive.

chapters.title: Ghost No More
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel burns Hazel's old identities in the plane's ashtray, one document at a time, and tells the crew the truth of who Hazel is. The beat is catharsis—the ghost dies so the person can board the rest of the life.

chapters.title: What We Carry
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, epilogue. Months later, Hazel, Ilya, Marisol, and Tomás stand outside a door in Porto with the sibling's name on it. Hazel knocks. The beat is quiet resolution: love against duty resolved into love chosen, family made, inheritance claimed.
